compatibility: Existing configuration, storage, session/event/result formats and raw-load activation retained.
Shared resume validates/restores before candidate binding; successful resume uses the same context and one storage read.
Checkpoint operations serialize, retaining immediate admission of first constructor/storage IO and custom restore/getState hooks.
save third argument additively accepts a deferred synchronous/asynchronous snapshot builder.
Teardown reports its first error after attempting other owned resources; original construction/load errors remain unchanged; shared skip-destroy ownership retained.
supportBoundaries: Loads require idle execution/host mutation. Independent contexts/backends require host concurrency coordination.
Custom plugins must honor serializable-state/restore contracts. Failed plugin rollback blocks saving until successful load or context rebuild; private/external hook side effects cannot be undone.
Restore hooks must not await checkpoint operations on their own context; those operations wait for restoration.
A throwing destructor remains responsible for its own private resources; framework cleans other reachable owned resources.
loadRaw intentionally remains an advanced unvalidated host operation.
